thesis: Existing IaaS conversion is demonstrated, but both sides depend on missing next-stage funding and cash evidence. Neither RPO scale nor EPS growth establishes infrastructure returns after obligations. Neutral recognizes realised operating growth while leaving present purchase value unproven.
strongest_counterexample: IaaS revenue $7.4bn grew121%, total revenue $19.3bn grew30%, and both GAAP and adjusted EPS improved, showing a real business beyond unconverted contracts.
invalidation_conditions: A matched primary infrastructure/debt/lease cash bridge reports surplus above zero after investment and service obligations, resolving the next-stage funding objection.
A subsequent comparable IaaS revenue growth rate at or below zero alongside negative post-investment cash would defeat the retained actual-conversion growth counterweight.
evidence_gaps: Current debt, leases, FCF and matched operating margin.
Funding and investment returns needed to deliver contracted activity.
Normalised valuation independent of vendor forward estimates.
decisive_factors: $664bn RPO is future activity rather than current cash.
Actual IaaS growth proves capability but not next-expansion funding.
Rate hurdle is general; company-specific repricing unquantified; mixed low-volume chart.
